messages:
maya: FluxLabs reporting sustained p99 token latency >400s on dedicated eu-c pool since 09:10 UTC. They also saw a billing token surge from retries. Any ideas on noisy neighbor? :grimacing:

sanjay: Can you share tenant id + a couple request ids? Model & sequence length? Also which MIG layout on that host — could be one hot slice hogging SMs.

maya: tenant=fluxlabs-eu, samples=[req_7f9e, req_a1b2], model=redwood-7b-chat, seq_len~1200, batch=1. Host has 3x7g.20gb slices. Excerpt from runtime logs: 
```log
[09:09:58] req req_7f9e START
[09:10:03] gpu0 sm_util=97% mem=18.7GB p99=1.1s
[09:10:09] response 429 timeout retried
```

jordan: Ops-bot timeline shows autoscaler evaluations at 09:12 and 09:18. First evaluation wanted +1 node but was blocked by reserved quota; second eval waited and then scaled at 09:25. So contention window lines up.

ops-bot: autoscaler: evaluate@09:12 -> desired_nodes=+1 -> scale_blocked (reserved_quota)
ops-bot: autoscaler: evaluate@09:18 -> desired_nodes=+1 -> still blocked
ops-bot: autoscaler: evaluate@09:25 -> scaled_up_nodes=1 (burst)

nico: Quick metric pulls for node eu-c-7: mig_sm_util: [slice0=97, slice1=11, slice2=13]. PCIe tx tail latency increased in same window. No power capping. Looks like one slice is doing heavy samplers/beam.

sanjay: Run these on the host and paste outputs, and check per-MIG counters: 
```bash
curl -s localhost:9100/metrics | grep mig_sm_util
sudo nvidia-smi mig -lgi
journalctl -u redwood-runtime --since "2026-03-16 09:00" | grep -i -E "evict|OOM|throttle"
```

maya: Pasted: mig_sm_util -> slice0=97, slice1=9, slice2=8. nvidia-smi shows 3 7g.20gb MIG instances. No eviction/ooms in journal.

emma: Customer impact: FluxLabs sees 3-5x p99 regressions and a retry storm that risks a billing overage this billing cycle. They want a mitigation path ASAP.

jordan: Short-term mitigations we can propose:
- move fluxlabs-eu to a single-tenant node (no other MIG slices) — needs ~30m maintenance
- shrink offending tenant to a smaller slice if model/quality allows
- grant temporary quota bump to allow autoscaler immediate scale
- apply a per-MIG soft concurrency cap to throttle heavy tenants gracefully

sanjay: Root cause likely: tenant (or co-located tenant) running heavy sampling/beam decode saturating SMs on one MIG slice, causing scheduler backpressure within the slice. Pool-level concurrency checks don't always surface slice-level saturation, so autoscaler decision was delayed.

maya: Repro steps for infra/devs to validate locally:
1) Deploy 3x 7g.20gb MIG slices on node
2) Run synthetic sampling job against one slice: seq=1200, temp=1.2, top_k/top_p heavy sampling, batch=1
3) Watch per-MIG sm_util and host-level p99 while keeping pool-level concurrency below autoscale threshold

nico: Action items:
- open internal infra ticket to request temporary reserved quota bump (owner: infra-team)
- add alert: mig_sm_util > 85% for 2m to prod (owner: monitoring)
- schedule tenant migration to single-tenant node if FluxLabs approves (owner: emma)
- evaluate implementing slice-level autoscale signals in next dev sprint (owner: eng-runtime)

jordan: I'll spin up an ops incident and tag infra + monitoring. If FluxLabs approves migration, target ETA ~2h for migration during off-peak. :white_check_mark:

maya: Thanks all. I'll present the options to the customer and ask if they want immediate migration vs quota bump. Will update this thread with customer reply. :pray:
